name: Larry Roberts

summary.text: Lawrence G. (Larry) Roberts was the ARPA Information Processing Techniques Office scientist who served as programme manager for the ARPANET, responsible for its management and design from 1966–67; the initial four-node network was deployed in late 1969. He was influenced by J.C.R. Licklider's network concept and worked under IPTO director Robert Taylor, who funded the project.

facts.claim: Roberts was the ARPA programme manager responsible for all aspects of the management and design of the ARPANET.
facts.quote: the program manager responsible for all aspects of the management and design of the ARPANET

facts.claim: Roberts was influenced by Licklider's 'Intergalactic Network' concept in designing the ARPANET.
The initial ARPANET was deployed in late 1969 with four host sites.
facts.quote: the initial ARPANET was deployed in late 1969 with four hosts

connections.claim: Roberts worked at ARPA's Information Processing Techniques Office as programme manager of the ARPANET.

openQuestions: Roberts's exact start date at ARPA (December 1966) and his later tenure as IPTO director (1969–1973) were not confirmed by sources found; the Computer History Museum's Roberts oral history or DARPA's own history would settle them.
The site frames IPTO as 'enclosure of the digital commons'; the sources record the ARPANET as a government-funded research network and do not address that characterisation.
